items.text: Stars can ask for a trade: a frustration meter, a Requests tab on the Trades page, and a price that falls while they wait
Manual trades get real offers: packages of starters and picks, and you can choose the protection of your own first-round pick
Young players' potential can change: breakouts and setbacks every summer
Injuries are counted in days and heal over the summer; long and season-ending injuries happen again
The calendar shows results while a long simulation runs, with the best performance of each day
Coach and GM firings, hirings and retirements make the news; rivalry stories are rarer and only for heated rivalries
A faster draft: Auto runs four times quicker, and one click sims to your next pick or, once your picks are done, to the end of the draft
Players look more like themselves on the court: passers pass, scorer-passers score more, creators who are not point guards run the offense
Stars can take 25 shots a game, but high volume now costs them percentage
A lone star on a weak team no longer scores 35-40 a night: the defense crowds him at the rim, bigs included
Post scorers with a good jumper use the fadeaway instead of always going to the rim
CPU teams choose their go-to scorers again: new stars become the first option, players who left no longer are
Long saves stay realistic: no rating inflation in the modern era, generated draft classes as strong as the curated ones, modern box scores
Generated players keep their role: centers no longer shoot threes like guards, guards no longer post up and block like centers
Stars who still play well age slowly and keep their role; veterans in their early 30s are no longer pushed out of the offense
Players who improve no longer all end up wanting every ball: after 25 seasons most stars had the maximum usage
Rebuilding teams are recognised during the season and give minutes to their young players
CPU trades no longer dry up in long saves, and lottery teams' future firsts are no longer priced as top-5 picks
Money: no contract above 35% of the cap, thrifty owners stay near the tax, no first-round pick to dump a small contract
Defensive Player of the Year weighs the team's record and defense, repeat winners face voter fatigue, blocks count as much as steals and the MVP rarely wins it too
Awards and history: a real Most Improved Player, a Rookie of the Year in the first season, a stricter Hall of Fame
Coaches grow only after good seasons, decline with age and retire; career records are counted correctly
Every team plays 82 games, and the playoffs play only a little slower than the regular season
Saves no longer store the same retired player several times
Smaller fixes: play-in labels in the league history, injury dates in career logs, trade impact numbers
The game no longer crashes at start when the zip was downloaded from GitHub
First public release: a fictional 2002 league, with real-name leagues as mods
CPU general managers with their own plans, wishes and trades
Contracts, free-agency auctions and the draft run by the same AI GMs
Day-by-day live simulation with a Stop button
League Analytics with rebounding, clutch and shot-zone stats
Saves are written all-or-nothing, with a backup copy
